title: Unresponsive
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is found unresponsive with pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression (RR <12), and decreased bowel sounds — the classic opioid toxidrome. There may be needle track marks. Immediate management: airway protection, bag-valve-mask ventilation, naloxone 0.4-2mg IV/IM/IN (repeat q2-3min, up to 10mg if no response). Naloxone is a pure opioid antagonist — rapidly reverses respiratory depression but can precipitate acute withdrawal (agitation, vomiting, diarrhea, piloerection). Short half-life (30-90 min) compared to many opioids → patient may become re-sedated → need for observation or naloxone infusion. Check glucose (coma cocktail). ECG (QT prolongation with methadone). Acetaminophen and salicylate levels if polysubstance ingestion suspected. After stabilization: screen for other substances, assess for aspiration pneumonitis, evaluate for rhabdomyolysis (prolonged down time). Offer substance use disorder resources and naloxone prescription for harm reduction. Psychiatry/addiction medicine consult.

stacks.label: Admit for observation
